rawSiteProfile.name: Ellwood Epps
rawSiteProfile.notes: Magento 1.x with custom "epps_interface" theme. Cloudflare is PASSIVE (no challenge). HTTP with any UA works. | needsPlaywright=FALSE. | Platform layout: <ol class="products-list"><li class="item"> (OLD Magento 1.x, not 2.x). Each <li.item> contains <table class="firearm-table"> with <td class="firearm-name"> holding the title+link. | Pagination: ?p=N query param. perPage=20. ".toolbar .amount" shows "Items 1 to 20 of N". | Sort: <select class="sort-by"> options include news_from_date. Newest-first URL = ?dir=desc&order=news_from_date. Verified — sort persists across ?p=2. | Default category order is admin "position"; do not rely on it for watermark — always apply sortParam. | Product count via /sitemap.xml (32,703 depth-1 product .html URLs after filtering static+category pages). HEAD-tested 5 random → 200. lastmod varies (1,573 unique dates) — sitemap IS usable for date-watermark. | Category totals (.toolbar-amount): /hunting/firearms.html=2,728, /hunting/ammunition.html=3,759, /hunting/accessories.html=16,997, /hunting/bow.html=58, /hunting/sets.html=3. Total hunting-relevant = 23,545. | Removed from catalogUrls: /hunting/parts.html (empty), /hunting/gunsmith.html (service page), /hunting/miscellaneous.html (not firearm-relevant). | No Magento REST API (/rest/V1/products → 404). No public JSON endpoint. robots.txt references only /sitemap.xml (flat, no index). | FIX 2026-04-06: Product URLs follow /catalog/product/view/id/NN/s/slug/category/NN/ — the trailing /category/ breadcrumb segment tripped the generic isNavUrl filter in GenericRetailAdapter and dropped 84% of products (firearms 1/20, accessories 0/20, ammunition 16/20). Fixed in generic-retail.ts by whitelisting the Magento 1 product-view URL pattern /catalog/product/view/id/\d+/ before the nav check in extractCatalogProducts. Post-fix extraction: firearms 20/20, accessories 20/20, ammunition 20/20, bow 20/20, sets 3/3. The existing ".products-list .item" selector was sufficient all along; extractTitle already picked up td.firearm-name via the [class*="name"] probe. The previous "JS-rendered" / "custom layout needs dedicated selector" claims were wrong — it was a URL-filter regression. | Audit dates: 2026-04-06.
